findings.text: The resume key conflates 'no recorded answer' with 'an answer whose facet confidence is 0.0'. The re-judge claim selects on coalesce(sf.score_data_access_confidence, 0.0) = 0.0 (graph_ops.py:517), and the explicit reset clears that field to absent (reset.py:480 clears _CODE_REJUDGE_FIELDS, of which score_data_access_confidence is one). A file whose content decision SUCCEEDS but returns a data-access confidence of 0.0 is written with confidence 0.0, so it never drains: within a pass the fresh-file guard stops re-judging it, but the next --rejudge-ingested pass re-claims and re-judges it again, indefinitely, because the reset no longer intervenes between passes. That is the same never-drains/over-count behaviour section 36 set out to remove, narrowed to files whose answer is a genuine zero confidence. The predicate is pre-existing and the plan names it, so this is a residual of the design rather than a done-when failure: the named tests use a non-zero confidence so none exercises the zero-answer path (test_code_ingested_rejudge.py:575,600). A one-line fix would drain on a field the re-judge always sets non-null (e.g. scored_at, or a dedicated re-judge marker) rather than on confidence.
